display.purpose: Screen-scale statements and empty-state moments. Rare by design.

headline.purpose: Large section moments and result statements.

title.purpose: Section headers, sheet titles, empty-state titles.

body.purpose: Transcripts, descriptions, message input. Content is capped at 760px wide so lines never sprawl.

body-small.purpose: Dense card content, status lines, banner text.

label.purpose: Pills, timestamps, captions, metadata. Sentence case, never uppercase.

code.purpose: File paths, commands, model ids, resource chips. Machine data only.

motion.name: press-spring
motion.value: scale(0.97) on press-in; spring release (RN spring, speed 50, bounciness 0); CSS: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
motion.purpose: Buttons and cards acknowledge touch without bounce.

motion.name: entrance-rise
motion.purpose: Once-per-screen-load entrance. Skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: approval-spring
motion.value: translateY 40px to 0 with slight overshoot (RN spring, speed 14, bounciness 7; CSS ~ cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), 320ms)
motion.purpose: The approval card's arrival, the one interruption the UI allows itself.

motion.name: pulse-ring
motion.value: radiating ring scales 1 to 3, opacity 0.6 to 0, 1500ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94) loop
motion.purpose: Live-status dot heartbeat. One pulsing element per screen, maximum.

motion.name: typing-dots
motion.purpose: Shown while the agent is composing.

motion.name: progress-sweep
motion.value: 2px bar sweeping under the header, 1400ms ease-in-out cubic loop

motion.name: skeleton-breath
motion.purpose: Loading placeholders breathe instead of shimmering.

breakpoints.name: content-max
breakpoints.purpose: Max width for lists, headers, and the transcript. Content never sprawls on tablets or web.

narrative.overview:
This is the flight deck of a quiet aircraft: a dark instrument panel, a handful of state lights, one operator watching a machine think. The system exists so a glance answers the only question that matters - what is the agent doing, and does it need me? - and so the two decisions that require a hand (approve, steer) are always one thumb-reach away. Nothing on the deck glows for decoration: every cyan, amber, coral, and mint light means something specific, and the moment it stops meaning something, it stops glowing.

Density is deliberately low. The phone is checked in passing, so each screen carries one dominant reading: a list of sessions with state rails, a transcript that breathes, a composer that waits. Depth comes from tone, not shadow - stepped navy surfaces separated by hairline seams, like panel sections bolted together.

The system explicitly rejects the AI-slop SaaS look (gradient accents, identical icon + title card grids, decorative glassmorphism, big-number hero metrics), the chat-app clone (messenger bubbles and chat chrome), and the admin dashboard (data-table-first screens, widget walls, dense toolbars). If any screen could pass for one of those, it has failed, regardless of polish.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first deck navy (#0A1219) with a frost-white day mode that mirrors it exactly.
Color is state, never decoration: cobalt = action, cyan = working, amber = needs you, coral = failed, mint = succeeded.
Flat with tonal layering and hairline seams. Zero shadows anywhere.
Tactile and alive: press-springs, pulsing status dots, a spring-up approval card - motion reserved for feedback and the one interruption the UI allows itself.
Instrument typography: one system sans (Spline Sans on web), tightened at scale; monospace only for machine data.

rules.name: The State-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Color communicates state or action, never mood. If a surface is cobalt, it is because it is the action on that screen. There are no tinted sections, no colored headers, no decorative accents.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: A screen may have exactly one pulsing element - the thing that needs you. Pulse is a heartbeat, not wallpaper.

rules.name: The Wash Rule
rules.body: State colors become surfaces only as washes (~12-13% alpha). Solid saturated fills are reserved for the one primary action and for dots.

rules.name: The Engraved Rule
rules.body: Anything at 22px or larger gets negative tracking (-0.4px or tighter). Large type is precision-machined, never airy.

rules.name: The Mono-as-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for machine data only - code, paths, identifiers. It is never used for mood, branding, or emphasis.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Zero shadows, ever. If a surface needs separation, use a lighter tone or a hairline seam. If a layer needs arrival, use motion.

rules.name: The State Border Rule
rules.body: Attention is carried by borders: the approval card wears a 1.5px amber ring (the only non-hairline border in the system); everything else keeps hairlines.

dos: Do reserve color for state and action: cobalt = action, cyan = working, amber = needs you, coral = failed, mint = succeeded. Nothing else gets color.
Do keep every touch target at 44px or larger, and use the radius steps: 8 (small), 14 (medium), 20 (large), pill for chips.
Do build depth with tone and seam: Deep Watch to Panel Navy to Lifted Panel, hairline borders, no exceptions.
Do give arrivals motion: spring-up for the approval card, slide-in for banners, 380ms fade-and-rise entrances once per screen load.
Do keep the approval card one thumb-reach from the composer, wearing its 1.5px amber ring.
Do stop every ambient animation under prefers-reduced-motion / AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled().
Do tighten tracking on anything 22px or larger (-0.4px or tighter). Engraved, not airy.
Do pair every status color with a label or dot shape so state never depends on color alone.
donts: Don't use drop shadows. If it looks like a card needs a shadow, the tone step or seam is wrong.
Don't let two things pulse on the same screen. One glow rule.
Don't reintroduce the AI-slop SaaS look: gradient accents, identical icon + title card grids, decorative glassmorphism, big-number hero metrics.
Don't build a chat-app clone: no messenger chrome, no bubble tails, no read receipts; the transcript is telemetry, not a conversation.
Don't build an admin dashboard: no data tables, no widget walls, no dense toolbars, no metric rows.
Don't tint sections, headers, or navigation with state colors, and never use gradient text.
Don't use monospace for mood. It is the voice of machine data only.
Don't fill a state surface with a solid saturated color - washes only (13% alpha or less), except the one primary action.
